What is a Root-Locus plot
A root locus plot is a graphical representation of the behavior of the roots of a system transfer function as a parameter varies.
The root locus plot is used to study the effect of changing the gain of a control system on the stability of the system and its response to disturbances.
The root locus plot is constructed by plotting the roots of the characteristic equation of the closed-loop transfer function as a parameter is varied.
The root locus plot shows how the poles move as the gain of the control system is increased or decreased.

The root locus plot provides valuable information about the stability of the system, including the number of poles in the right half of the complex plane, which determines the stability of the system, and the number of poles on the imaginary axis, which determines the damping ratio and the rate of decay of the response.
The root locus plot also provides information about the response of the system to a step input, including the rise time, settling time, and overshoot.
In conclusion, the root locus plot is a powerful tool for control system design and analysis, providing valuable information about the stability and response of a control system.
